- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% and add a 2–3 day lagged mean-reversion buffer.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates 30d horizon; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 14-day average to avoid overconfidence.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits lagged response; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend by aligning with sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment > 0.1, add 0.5–1.0 to forecast).  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 30d price drops >10% from 18d high), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 1–2% upward bias to forecast to counteract underestimation.
